ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: The Sun God Car has a huge pendulum hung by a four-legged support and swinging, and tourists are fixed on the large disk A below the pendulum, as shown in the figure. The swinging amplitude of the pendulum can reach 120° on each side. Six high-power asynchronous drive motors start at the same time, creating an acceleration of 4.3 g for tourists, and it can fly up to a height of 15 stories. If the rotation of disk A is not considered, according to the above information, which of the following statements is correct?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text: When the pendulum swings up and down to the lowest point, tourists must be in an overweight experience

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: in the figure, an amusement facility can be seen. On the right side there is a tall support, and near the top of the support hangs a swing arm/pendulum structure; at the end of the swing arm there is a large circular disk, labeled A beside it, and tourists should be fixed on this disk. The overall structure corresponds to the “Sun God Car” mentioned in the stem, swinging up and down in a vertical plane like a simple pendulum. Then reason: the problem requires not considering the rotation of disk A, and only considering the up-and-down swing of the pendulum. Thus the tourists can be regarded as objects that move in vertical circular motion with disk A around the upper suspension point. When the pendulum swings to the lowest point, the centripetal acceleration required for circular motion points toward the upper suspension point, namely upward. The tourists are subject to gravity downward and also to the support/restraint force of the seat or restraint device on them. In order for the resultant force to be upward and provide centripetal acceleration, the restraint force must be greater than gravity, so the “support force” felt by the tourists is greater than their own weight, which is an overweight state.
